page: Amazon Web Services r8g.metal-24xl is a bare-metal memory-optimized instance powered by custom AWS Graviton4 processors built on the arm64 Neoverse-V2 architecture. The system delivers 96 physical cores across 96 dedicated vCPUs with 1 thread per core running at 2.8 GHz, supported by 2 MB of L2 cache per core and 36 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Networking throughput reaches a 40 Gbps baseline. The configuration excludes local storage and discrete GPUs, meaning all persistent and operational storage must be attached over the network.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded scaling and memory performance. The server achieves a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 163,907.12 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 26,252.0, placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated instances. Memory benchmarks corroborate this profile, demonstrating 481.15 GB/sec of uncached read throughput and 218.18 GB/sec of write throughput on large blocks, alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3,409.51. In-memory data store workloads excel, with Redis achieving 198.34 million SET operations per second and PassMark database operations reaching 47,714.55. Software compilation in Clang and physics simulations also land in the top decile.

Single-core performance is typical for Arm-based efficiency designs, registering average scores across Geekbench and stress-ng tests. Hardware encryption performance remains midrange despite native AES acceleration, as architectural x86 extensions like AVX-512 are absent. Text generation on smaller language models is limited due to the absence of dedicated accelerators, though larger quantized model generation remains viable using system memory. Bare-metal deployment removes hypervisor overhead, maximizing direct hardware utilization.

The r8g.metal-24xl offers strong resource efficiency for memory-intensive enterprise footprints requiring predictable physical core isolation. It is ideally suited for in-memory databases like Redis, massive relational database management systems, big data analytics engines, and high-concurrency microservices architectures.

The system contains no discrete GPUs and relies entirely on external network storage. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier throughput in multi-core compute and memory-bound metrics, recording 481.15 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth, 198.34 million Redis SET operations per second, and 163,907.12 in stress-ng multi-core execution.
